clue.text: Physical sort of dance music for city

parts.note: concrete means real and tangible, existing in physical form
jungle is a fast, bass-heavy style of electronic dance music

explanation.surface: A dance-music fan asks which tangible style of music suits urban life.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a big city seen as harsh and crowded with buildings.

clue.text: Killer briefly in company

parts.note: the poisonous gas is written briefly as its chemical formula, CO, which is also the abbreviation of company

explanation.surface: A murderer joins a firm for a short spell.
explanation.walkthrough: The killer is a poisonous gas whose formula, CO, is the same as the short form of 'company'; so the gas, written briefly, is a company.
explanation.definitionFit: This colourless, odourless gas is a notorious silent killer from faulty boilers and car exhausts.

clue.text: Simple cover for East End local

indicators.note: the word for simple wraps round, so covers, the letter that follows

indicators.note: the end of East is its final letter

explanation.surface: An unsophisticated disguise worn by a Londoner from the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East End' looks like the London district, but it means the last letter of 'East'.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is a person born in a place, someone indigenous to it.

clue.text: Proportion of celebrations

indicators.note: the answer is part of the word celebrations, taken out of it

explanation.surface: Asking what share of the festivities something takes up.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses one quantity relative to another, which is a proportion.

clue.text: Somewhere in North Africa most of Isis is tackled by swimmer

indicators.note: the fish takes on, grips round, the cut-down word

parts.note: a tuna is a fish, so a swimmer

indicators.note: the word Isis loses its last letter

explanation.surface: An Isis-related news item from North Africa in which a swimmer tackles a militant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Isis' tempts as the militant group or Oxford's river; 'most of' drops its final letter, and 'is tackled by' sets what is left inside the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia is a country on the Mediterranean coast of North Africa.

clue.text: See 1 across
On the map Sunderland is pants

definitions.meaning: on a map the town of Sunderland sits on the river Wear, so it is written below (beneath) the Wear
in British English pants are knickers or briefs, items worn next to the skin

explanation.surface: A grumpy verdict that Sunderland, as seen on the map, is rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' is British slang for rubbish, which the surface uses; the definition is pants as undergarments. Sunderland is a city in north-east England at the mouth of the river Wear.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage pants means knickers or briefs, clothing worn beneath trousers.

clue.text: Play with Lego and seem happy

explanation.surface: A child plays with Lego bricks and looks cheerful.

clue.text: Spinning round rubbish in circle

clue.text: Characters in Solzhenitsyn chronicle go together

clue.text: Oboe, violin up 50% – devious for sure

clue.text: Tries desperately to take another exam

clue.text: Delight in petition of course

clue.text: Browsers need her sign before rainstorm

clue.text: He's in the Czech Republic, initially moving out, ignoring my place in Paris

explanation.walkthrough: 'moving out' looks like the move; only the initial letters of 'moving out, ignoring' are used.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means at my home, which suits a Parisian speaking of their own place.

clue.text: See 1 down

clue.text: Start of computer reboot could be a revolution

clue.text: 21 across — cunning device
